# Tool inventory — the bundled Teradata MCP server as this plugin exposes it

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/render_references.py from scripts/data/mcp_tools.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Purpose: the exact tool, prompt and resource names the `teradata` server registers, grouped as upstream groups them, so a skill or agent can name a tool without guessing.

- Package: `teradata-mcp-server` version `0.2.6`
- Wheel sha256: `8e93870a76231bd736f0369d3a085f1d78814c38466fd36534ba183eac63422c`
- Server key in `.mcp.json`: `teradata`
- Full tool-name prefix: `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__<tool>`
- Groups: 13; tools listed: 65; prompts listed: 13; resources: 4
- Tools registered by a core install (no extras, default profile) at capture time: 47
- Inventory source: captured from a live `tools/list` + `prompts/list` + `resources/list` against the vendored wheel; groups that register only with extras or extra environment are listed from the upstream source.
- Longest fully namespaced tool name: 68 characters — the MCP tool names themselves stay under 64 characters; Claude Code prefixes them client-side with the plugin/server scope. Seven namespaced names run 65-68 characters (bar_manageDiskFileTargetGroup, bar_manageDsaDiskFileSystem, chat_aggregatedCompleteChat, qlty_rowsWithMissingValues, sql_Retrieve_Cluster_Queries, tdvs_grant_user_permission, tdvs_revoke_user_permission). Measured 2026-09-05: a 67-character namespaced name loads its schema and executes against the database, so name length is not a reason to leave a tool out of an agent tools: list.

Which groups load is decided by the server profile (`config/profiles.yml`; default `tv_all`) and by the optional extras installed with the local server. A tool that is not loaded is not callable, however it is named here.

## Safety classification

Held read-only by a PreToolUse hook (ONE statement, starting SELECT/WITH/EXPLAIN/SHOW/HELP; a blocked verb anywhere else denies the call, except after a leading EXPLAIN, which returns a plan and executes nothing — so EXPLAIN DELETE / INSERT / UPDATE / MERGE are allowed; `TERADATA_SQL_GUARD_MODE=audit` logs instead of denying):

- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__base_readQuery`

Raise an approval prompt before running. The SQL-executing tools prompt only when the statement is destructive — DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE, INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE, ALTER, MODIFY, RENAME, REPLACE (VIEW/MACRO/PROCEDURE/…), GIVE, CREATE DATABASE/USER, GRANT, REVOKE, ABORT SESSION (a statement that is only DROP FOREIGN TABLE is exempt as metadata-only, and that exemption is applied per STATEMENT, never to a whole compound call); the vector-store, backup and pipeline tools always prompt; `TERADATA_ALLOW_WRITES=0` denies all writes:

- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__base_writeQuery`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__base_dynamicQuery`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__base_saveDDL`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__sql_Execute_Full_Pipeline`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__rag_Execute_Workflow`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__tdvs_destroy`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__tdvs_update`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__tdvs_revoke_user_permission`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__tdvs_grant_user_permission`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__bar_manageJob`

When the server runs with `PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE=true`, most tools are reached through these instead, and the hooks classify `execute_tool` calls by the inner `tool_name`:

- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__search_tool`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__execute_tool`
- `mcp__plugin_teradata-vantage_teradata__base_readQuery`

These guards are mistake-prevention on the analyst tools, not a security boundary; the database's own rights model is the boundary.
